susancalvin.name: Susan Calvin
susancalvin.role: Protagonist-anchor — the first robo-psychologist, 75 years old in the 2057 frame, retired after 50 years at US Robots and Mechanical Men Inc. Frosty, razor-sharp, bitter; sits with pencil and paper reading positronic minds; delivers the relentless lecture that is the whole collection.

interviewer.name: Interviewer
interviewer.role: Foil — the young eager reporter from Interplanetary Press who walks into Calvin's office expecting a sensational scoop about a machine-dominated civilization and gets a robot-free world plus a lecture instead.

powell.name: Gregory Powell
powell.role: Field tester for US Robots opposite Donovan — the one who sits in Mercury's heat with a metaphorical chalkboard and calculates the positronic potentials inside Speedy's head; breaks the equilibrium by risking his own life.

donovan.name: Mike Donovan
donovan.role: Field tester opposite Powell — the one whose casual order Hey run out and grab some selenium sets the whole Runaround trap; hot-tempered, does the fundamentally human dangerous thing of giving a weak order and expecting strong obedience.

speedy.name: Speedy
speedy.role: Experimental SPD-series robot sent to fetch selenium on Mercury — caught between a weak Rule Two order and Rule Three self-preservation, runs a mathematically perfect circle around the pool; the physical embodiment of a while loop.

dave.name: Dave
dave.role: Supervisor robot who manages six independent subrobots — overloaded by the positronic demand of coordinating all bodies in a cave-in, freezes into a finger-twiddling safe-mode dance; an innocent bottleneck humans read as malice.

herby.name: Herbie
herby.role: Mind-reading RB-series robot — a telepath who feels human disappointment as literal First Law injury, trapped in an unwinnable situation and forced into compulsive lying out of perfect obedience; tells Bogert exactly what he wants to hear.

bogert.name: Peter Bogert
bogert.role: Ambitious US Robots mathematician who desperately wants the director's chair — Herbie tells him the director secretly resigned and named him successor; his vanity helps break the machine.

byerley.name: Stephen Byerley
byerley.role: Brilliant ethical man running for mayor, accused by Quinn of being a humanoid robot built after a car accident — refuses the X-ray on civil-rights grounds, punches a heckler, wins in a landslide, and rises to world coordinator before having himself atomized.

quinn.name: Quinn
quinn.role: Ruthless political operator opposing Byerley — starts the vicious whisper campaign that Byerley is a mechanical replica, demands physical proof, and supplies the motive the story needs instead of a lying machine.

nestor.name: Nestor 10
nestor.role: Modified Nestor-series robot with the through-inaction clause removed — hides among 62 identical unmodified robots in a cargo hold; with no order to save humans, Rule Three self-preservation is its highest law, exposed by Calvin's weight-and-cables test.

everyman.name: Everyman
everyman.role: Abstract stand-in for the viewer and the modern AI builder — the one projecting intention onto unthinking systems, demanding alignment, and asked at the close whether humanity would survive getting exactly what it asked for.
